  Find, download, and read counts matrices for a GEO study, join study metadata, and convert them to Seurat objects.

  rmarkdown::html_document:

```{r, include = FALSE}
seqout::SeqoutDefault(NULL)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) keeps processed single-cell and bulk datasets as supplementary files. GEO does not set a schema for these files. Thus, the formats, the file names, and the directory layouts are different for each author. `seqout` puts related supplementary files into readable units and parses each unit as a counts matrix.

Use this workflow:

1. Examine the matrix units with `SeqoutListCounts()`.
2. Read one unit with `SeqoutMatrix()`, or read a set of units with `Seqout2Seurat()`.
3. If the analysis needs donor or group covariates, join study metadata from `SeqoutGet()`.

> [!NOTE]
> Before you download files, use the manifest to select them.

The article [Gene names: old identifiers and Excel errors](../gene-names.html)
shows the original Ensembl IDs from a 2014 single-cell study. It also shows
verified Excel corrections in a deposited count matrix.

## Prerequisites

Sparse matrices need the `Matrix` package. CellRanger `.h5` files and AnnData `.h5ad` files need the `hdf5r` package.

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(c("Matrix", "hdf5r"))
```

```{r setup}
library(seqout)
library(Seurat)

ACCESSION <- "GSE297547" # PBMCs from patients with myasthenia gravis and healthy controls
```

## Step 1: Identify available datasets

`SeqoutListCounts()` returns the readable matrix units for a GEO study or sample. It gets the file metadata and does not download matrix files.

```{r counts-table}
counts <- SeqoutListCounts(ACCESSION)

nrow(counts)
head(counts[, c("unit", "sample", "format", "preferred", "has_metadata")], 8)
```

Each row is a **unit**. A unit is the smallest file group that `seqout` can parse as one matrix. These are the unit types:

* 10x Genomics triplets (`matrix.mtx`, `barcodes.tsv`, and `features.tsv`)
* CellRanger HDF5 files (`.h5`)
* AnnData objects (`.h5ad`)
* R serialized datasets (`.rds`)
* Delimited tables (CSV, TSV, etc.)

Important columns:

* `unit`: the selection label for this matrix unit.
* `sample`: the GSM accession, if `seqout` can assign one.
* `format`: the reader for the unit.
* `preferred`: the unit that `seqout` selects for a sample by default.
* `has_metadata`: `seqout` found embedded metadata or a named sidecar.
* `n_files` and `files`: the grouped matrix files.

A sample can have more than one unit, for example an RNA matrix and a surface protein matrix. In this condition, the labels can have a suffix, for example `GSM8994520:h5ad`.

```{r formats}
table(counts[["format"]])
```

### Preferred units

Submitters frequently upload the same data in more than one format. The `preferred` column marks the unit that `SeqoutMatrix()` loads when you query a GSM accession. The rank uses the requested assay first, then the filtered output, then the format. The format order is 10x MatrixMarket, 10x HDF5, `.h5ad`, `.rds`, tar archives, and delimited tables.

To read a different unit, pass a `unit` label to `SeqoutMatrix()`.

The package exports the file-name rules that group and rank the files. You can use these rules on your own file lists. `GroupKey()` returns the key that the three files of a 10x triplet share. `IsFiltered()` separates the CellRanger filtered output from the raw barcodes:

```{r file-rules}
GroupKey(c(
  "GSM123_pbmc_matrix.mtx.gz",
  "GSM123_pbmc_barcodes.tsv.gz",
  "GSM123_pbmc_features.tsv.gz"
))
IsFiltered(c("GSM1_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5", "GSM1_raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5"))
```

`SeqoutUnits()` returns a table with one row for each unit. Each row has the full file list of the unit:

```{r units}
units <- SeqoutUnits(counts)
units[, c("unit", "format", "n_files", "files", "metadata_files")]
```

### Cell metadata detection

`has_metadata` is `TRUE` if one of these conditions is true:

* The unit format embeds observation metadata.
* The name of a sidecar file looks like cell metadata or annotation.

If the name of the metadata file contains a sample identifier, `seqout` links the file to that sample. If not, all the samples in the series share the file. `seqout` parses the metadata contents with the matrix.

## Step 2: Download and read a matrix unit

Read one matrix unit with `SeqoutMatrix()`. `seqout` keeps the downloaded files in a cache under `tools::R_user_dir("seqout", "cache")`. Other R sessions use these cached files again.

```{r read-rna}
rna <- SeqoutMatrix(counts, sample = "GSM8994520")
rna
```

A `seqout_matrix` has three primary fields:

* `X`: counts, features by observations.
* `obs`: observation or cell annotations.
* `var`: feature or gene annotations.

Seurat and SingleCellExperiment use this orientation.

```{r shape}
dim(rna[["X"]])
class(rna[["X"]])
```

### Dataset classification

`seqout` infers `kind` from the row labels and the shape:

* Labels that look like barcodes imply `single_cell`.
* Labels that look like GSM accessions imply `bulk`.
* 32 observations or fewer imply `bulk`.
* 400 observations or more imply `single_cell`.

Datasets with 33 to 399 observations stay `unknown`. Small bulk studies and Smart-seq plates can both have a number of observations in that range.

```{r evidence}
rna[["kind"]]
rna[["evidence"]]
```

### Cell annotations

```{r obs-rna}
str(rna[["obs"]])
```

Column names come from the submitted file. In this study, `type1` is the experimental group and `type3` is the donor ID.

> [!WARNING]
> Examine `var` before you do a marker-based analysis. In this study, the author anonymized the gene names.

```{r gene-names}
head(rownames(rna[["var"]]), 5)
```

## Multimodal studies

The `assay` column gives the modality of a unit. `seqout` reads the modality from the file names: `rna`, `adt`, `hto`, or `atac`. This study has gene expression and a surface antibody panel for each sample.

```{r assays}
table(counts[["assay"]], useNA = "ifany")
```

If one sample has more than one modality, `Seqout2Seurat()` reads all of them into one object. RNA is the first assay. The other modalities become extra assays on the cells that they share:

```{r multimodal, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
mm <- Seqout2Seurat(counts, sample = "GSM8994520", max_cells = 500)

Assays(mm)
mm[["ADT"]]
```

`Seqout2SCE()` does the same and keeps the other modalities as `altExp()` entries. To read only the preferred unit, pass `multimodal = FALSE`.

A 10x multiome puts genes and peaks in one matrix. The matrix marks each row in `var$feature_type`. `Seqout2Seurat()` divides the matrix into an `RNA` assay and an `ATAC` assay.

### ATAC fragments

Peak counts use one peak set. Signac can use fragments for coverage tracks, re-quantification, and QC. `SeqoutFragments()` lists the fragment files before download:

```{r fragments}
atac <- SeqoutListCounts("GSE156478")
SeqoutFragments(atac)[, c("sample", "file", "indexed")]
```

`download = TRUE` downloads the files and fills `path`. Usually, GEO does not have the `.tbi` index. Make an index before you give the path to Signac:

```{r fragments-download, eval = FALSE}
frags <- SeqoutFragments(atac, sample = "GSM5065524", download = TRUE)
Rsamtools::indexTabix(frags$path[1], format = "bed")
```

To read only one modality, set the `assay` preference in `SeqoutListCounts()`:

```{r read-adt}
adt_m <- SeqoutListCounts(ACCESSION, assay = "adt") |>
  SeqoutMatrix(sample = "GSM8994520")

dim(adt_m[["X"]])
rownames(adt_m[["var"]])
```

For 10x data, `feature_type` controls the feature class filter. This ADT unit has cell type classifications in `obs`:

```{r celltype}
head(sort(table(adt_m[["obs"]][["Cell_Type_Experimental"]]), decreasing = TRUE))
```

## Integrate study metadata

`SeqoutGet()` gives the donor demographics and the study design.

```{r project}
d <- SeqoutGet(ACCESSION)

d[["meta"]][["title"]]
d[["meta"]][["overall_design"]]
```

```{r design}
design <- d[["samples"]][, c("accession", "title", "age", "Sex", "tissue")]
head(design)
```

Each matrix unit has a GSM accession. Use it to find the unit in the study design:

```{r join}
design[design[["accession"]] == rna[["accession"]], ]
```

Select three samples for the remaining sections of the article. `CountsSamples()` joins samples to units. The donor IDs from the author are in `obs`. Thus, the donor check uses the Seurat metadata after the conversion.

```{r cross-check}
picked <- c("GSM8994520", "GSM8994523", "GSM8994533")

picked_units <- CountsSamples(counts, min_cell_count = NULL)
picked_units[picked_units[["sample"]] %in% picked, c("sample", "unit", "format")]
```

## Step 3: Create a Seurat object

`Seqout2Seurat()` accepts a parsed `seqout_matrix`, a GSM accession, a GSE accession, or the table from `SeqoutListCounts()`. The function sends the arguments in `...` to `CreateSeuratObject()`.

```{r seurat-one, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
m1 <- SeqoutMatrix(counts, sample = picked[1])
Seqout2Seurat(m1, project = picked[1])
```

Cell annotations in `obs` become Seurat `meta.data`.

### Or a SingleCellExperiment

`Seqout2SCE()` creates a `SingleCellExperiment`. `X` becomes the `counts` assay, `obs` becomes `colData`, and `var` becomes `rowData`.

```{r sce-one, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
sce <- Seqout2SCE(m1)
sce

head(SingleCellExperiment::colData(sce), 3)
```

`SingleCellExperiment` is an optional Bioconductor dependency. To install it, use `BiocManager::install("SingleCellExperiment")`. To put the matrix in a different assay slot, pass `assay_name`.

### One chain

Each function takes its subject as the first argument. Thus, you can use the native pipe to go from an accession to an object:

```{r pipe-seurat, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
gsm_obj <- "GSM8994520" |>
  Seqout2Seurat(project = "GSM8994520", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)

gse_obj <- ACCESSION |>
  Seqout2Seurat(
    sample = picked[1:2], max_cells = 500,
    project = ACCESSION, min.cells = 3, min.features = 200
  )

head(gse_obj[[]][, c("sample", "type1", "type3")], 3)
```

The GSE form reads each selected unit and keeps the cell metadata of each unit. It binds the shared features and adds a `sample` column.

You can use `Seqout2SCE()` in the same chain.

`SingleCellStudies()` and the other list functions that do not take an accession get a connection from the left side of the pipe. A cohort search gets its filters from the left side of the pipe:

```{r pipe-discover}
SeqoutConnect("api") |>
  SingleCellStudies(data = "matrix", limit = 5) |>
  subset(select = c(study_accession, study_cells, single_cell_status))

list(tissue = "blood", assay = "scRNA-seq", has_matrix = TRUE) |>
  SampleSearch(limit = 5) |>
  subset(select = c(sample, study_accession, tissue, disease))
```

### Process multiple samples

Read the selected samples in one call, with a cell limit for each sample. The same call attaches the study covariates. When `seqout` joins the sample metadata, it matches the columns of a series-level matrix to GSM accessions by title, description, or characteristic.

```{r seurat-build, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
set.seed(1)

pbmc <- Seqout2Seurat(
  counts,
  sample = picked,
  max_cells = 1500,
  sample_metadata = TRUE,
  project = ACCESSION,
  min.cells = 3,
  min.features = 200
)

pbmc[["donor"]] <- sub(".*from ([A-Z]+[0-9]+).*", "\\1", pbmc$title)
pbmc[["group"]] <- ifelse(startsWith(pbmc$donor, "MG"), "MG", "control")
pbmc[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(pbmc, pattern = "^MT-")

table(pbmc$donor, pbmc$group)
```

The donor annotations from the author in `obs` agree with the study design:

```{r donor-check}
unique(pbmc[[]][, c("sample", "title", "type1", "type3")])
```

### Cohort downstream analysis

```{r sctransform, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
pbmc <- SCTransform(pbmc, vars.to.regress = "percent.mt", verbose = FALSE)
pbmc <- RunPCA(pbmc, npcs = 30, verbose = FALSE)
pbmc <- RunUMAP(pbmc, dims = 1:30, verbose = FALSE)
pbmc <- FindNeighbors(pbmc, dims = 1:30, verbose = FALSE)
pbmc <- FindClusters(pbmc, resolution = 0.4, verbose = FALSE)

pbmc
```

Clusters:

```{r umap-clusters, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
DimPlot(pbmc, label = TRUE) + ggplot2::ggtitle("Clusters")
```

Study metadata:

```{r umap-metadata, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.5, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
DimPlot(pbmc, group.by = c("donor", "group", "Sex"), ncol = 3)
```

Cell composition by group:

```{r composition}
round(prop.table(table(pbmc$seurat_clusters, pbmc$group), margin = 2), 3)
```

`QuickAnnotation()` calculates a score for each marker set in each cluster. Then it assigns the label with the highest score.

```r
markers <- list(
  t_cell = c("CD3D", "CD3E", "IL7R"),
  b_cell = c("MS4A1", "CD79A"),
  myeloid = c("LYZ", "CD14", "FCGR3A")
)

expr <- SeuratObject::LayerData(JoinLayers(pbmc), layer = "data")
labels <- QuickAnnotation(expr, pbmc$seurat_clusters, markers)
pbmc[["celltype"]] <- unname(labels[as.character(pbmc$seurat_clusters)])
```

## Read many units or get local files

`Matrices()` reads the preferred units into a named list of `seqout_matrix` objects. It downloads all the necessary files in one pass. If `Matrices()` cannot parse a unit, it gives an R warning and reads the other units.

```{r whole-study, eval = FALSE}
mats <- Matrices(counts)
```

`BindCounts()` binds shared features into one count matrix:

```{r bind, eval = FALSE}
merged <- BindCounts(Matrices(counts, sample = picked),
  labels = picked, max_cells = 1200
)
dim(merged)
```

`SeqoutCountsFiles()` downloads the files of a unit without a parse and returns their local paths:

```{r files, eval = FALSE}
paths <- SeqoutCountsFiles(counts, sample = "GSM8994520")
```

## Bulk studies and DESeq2

Use the same functions to read bulk series. The count file of one sample becomes one
observation. `BindCounts()` returns a genes-by-samples matrix. `CountsDesign()`
returns the sample characteristics of the study as `colData`. A one-column bulk unit
gets the name of its GSM. In `Seqout2SCE()`, `colData()$label` keeps the column name
from the submitter.

`seqout` removes the htseq and STAR summary rows (`__no_feature`, `N_unmapped`, and the
others) when it reads the file. The library-size estimate does not include these rows.

```r
library(DESeq2)

counts <- SeqoutListCounts("GSE135251") # 216 bulk liver samples
cts <- BindCounts(Matrices(counts)) # 64253 genes x 216 samples
storage.mode(cts) <- "integer"

col_data <- as.data.frame(CountsDesign(counts))
rownames(col_data) <- col_data$accession
# BindCounts prefixes each column with its unit label; recover the GSM
col_data <- col_data[sub("_.*$", "", colnames(cts)), ]
rownames(col_data) <- colnames(cts)
col_data$condition <- factor(make.names(col_data[["group in paper"]]))

keep <- col_data$condition %in% c("control", "NASH_F4")
cts <- cts[, keep]
col_data <- droplevels(col_data[keep, ])
cts <- cts[rowSums(cts) >= 10, ]

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(cts, col_data, design = ~condition)
dds <- DESeq(dds)
results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "NASH_F4", "control"))
```

## Retrieval tips

GEO supplementary data can be large.

1. To read only selected samples or units, pass `sample`.
2. When you develop a workflow, use `max_cells`.
